source.title: UEGP: Unified Expert-Guided Pre-training for Knowledge Rekindle
source.authors: Yu-Tao Mou; Kexiang Wang; Jian-He Lin; De-Hong Ma; Jun Fan; Dai-Ting Shi; Zhi-Cong Cheng; Simiu Gu; Dawei Yin; Wei-Ran Xu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream-task scores for different model sizes, a different measure and setting from scaling-law tests of held-out pretraining loss. It does not fit or test scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. for background but reports no held-out pretraining cross-entropy sweep, fitted power laws, extrapolation test, or compute-optimal allocation test. Its own size comparisons and downstream scores bear narrowly on V6. Results comparing expert-guided training variants are included only where they also compare model sizes; the MoEGP checkpoints at one student size do not test a size effect.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper on knowledge-rekindle distillation (UEGP). It cites Kaplan et al. only as background. Its size comparisons are off-the-shelf BERT-base vs BERT-large (12 vs 24 layers) and ERNIE 12 vs 48 layers, used as baselines or as student backbones for its own method. It reports no held-out loss, no fitted or predictive relationship and no scale sweep, so it does not test V6 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that UEGP (knowledge distillation plus MLM re-pretraining guided by fine-tuned experts) improves fine-tuned models on GLUE and on industrial re-ranking without extra labels. They also claim gains grow with student and teacher size, and that MLM acts as a regularizer. They draw no scaling-law conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses expert-guided pre-training with knowledge distillation and MLM, followed by task-specific fine-tuning. It compares a small number of BERT/ERNIE sizes using downstream metrics, rather than fitting held-out language-model loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream outcomes are reported for different teacher and student model sizes; the paper also varies expert-guided pre-training objectives and steps, but those comparisons do not test scaling-law fit dependence.

fits_no_version.finding: Gains from expert-guided distillation grow with student and teacher size on QNLI and SST-2 (4, 12 and 24 layers). The trend is not monotonic: on QNLI, 24-24 scores 92.10 vs 12-24 at 92.54.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefit of knowledge-distillation-based re-pretraining grows with teacher and student model size.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024
record.problems: The size comparisons cover only a small set of model sizes and downstream tasks; they do not measure held-out pretraining loss or establish a fitted, predictive scale relationship over several orders of magnitude. Table 1 reports results averaged over three random runs and p < 0.01 under t-test, but per-task uncertainty details are not given.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results exceeding the 60-row limit. MoEGP comparisons at a fixed BERT-large student size were not recorded as scale tests; they vary training strategy/checkpoint rather than model size.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or regime scaling law.
No predictive relation of downstream score to scale or loss. Only two or three public checkpoint sizes appear, as baselines.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V6 supports labels was rejected. The base/large comparisons are baselines from public checkpoints, and the authors' own scale remark is an argument, not a measured scaling relation. V6 requires predictability across scale, which two sizes cannot show.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss measured against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No predictions from small runs or comparisons with larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token counts.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
No other-modality or alternative-training-regime scaling-law test.
The comparisons do not fit a predictive relationship, test pretraining-loss-to-downstream performance, or establish predictability over several orders of magnitude.
No analysis of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending.
